title: The emerging roles of the gut microbiome in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation

items.quote: Increased susceptibility to bacterial infections such as Pseudomonas, Enterobacter, Klebsiella, parasites, fungi, and reactivation of latent viruses
items.location: body: Current concepts in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
items.note: Non-GVHD outcome: opportunistic infection after allo-HSCT, not tied to GVHD in the statement. [7]

items.quote: Bifidobacterium spp. is associated with delayed tumor progression and increased responses to programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) checkpoint blockade
items.note: Non-transplant context (checkpoint immunotherapy) and no GVHD outcome; the next sentence on Bacteroides spp. and CTLA-4 blockade fails for the same reason. [32], [33]

items.quote: The decreased abundances of Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus, together with an increased abundance of Enterobacteriaceae are the key microbiota shifts in elderly individuals
items.location: body: Significant differences between HSCT in murine models and humans
items.note: Composition shift with aging; no GVHD link in the statement. [55]

items.quote: transfer of Christensenella minuta to germ-free mice significantly reduced adiposity gain
items.location: body: Significant differences between HSCT in murine models and humans
items.note: Non-transplant context and non-GVHD outcome (adiposity); the preceding Bifidobacteria aging-biomarker sentence fails for the same reason. [64]

items.quote: High microbiome diversity correlates with better survival rate, lower incidence and severity of GVHD
items.location: body: Methodological approach to study intestinal microbiota
items.note: Diversity only; whole-community measure is not a target. [59,60,83,84]

items.quote: some pathogenic bacterial taxa have been shown to increase in the GVHD recipients such as Enterococcaceae, Akkermansia muciniphila, and Lactobacillales
items.location: body: Microbiota modification and HSCT outcomes
items.note: Family rank; the 4.1 pathobiont list names Enterococcus (genus) only, so assigned 0 rather than 4b. Two sentences later the review calls Enterococcaceae essential for GI integrity after radiation (skipped, non-GVHD outcome); direction kept exacerbating.

items.quote: some pathogenic bacterial taxa have been shown to increase in the GVHD recipients such as Enterococcaceae, Akkermansia muciniphila, and Lactobacillales
items.location: body: Microbiota modification and HSCT outcomes

fields.mechanism_as_named: Akkermansia muciniphila increased in GVHD recipients

items.note: Figure 2 places A. muciniphila beside the mucus layer, but the text gives no mechanism for it and the figure is uncited, so 0.

items.quote: some pathogenic bacterial taxa have been shown to increase in the GVHD recipients such as Enterococcaceae, Akkermansia muciniphila, and Lactobacillales
items.location: body: Microbiota modification and HSCT outcomes

items.quote: Blautia has been shown as the beneficial bacterial genus for HSCT
items.location: body: Microbiota modification and HSCT outcomes
items.note: Non-GVHD outcome: benefit is stated for HSCT generally, with no GVHD outcome in the statement. Promote if 'beneficial for HSCT' is read as GVHD. [88]

items.quote: the correlation of increased GVHD with reduced abundances of some bacterial genera such as Faecalibacterium, Bacteroides, and Parabacteroides
items.location: body: Microbiota modification and HSCT outcomes

fields.mechanism_as_named: Reduced Faecalibacterium correlates with increased GVHD

items.location: body: Microbiota modification and HSCT outcomes

fields.mechanism_as_named: Reduced Bacteroides correlates with increased GVHD

items.quote: the correlation of increased GVHD with reduced abundances of some bacterial genera such as Faecalibacterium, Bacteroides, and Parabacteroides
items.location: body: Microbiota modification and HSCT outcomes

fields.mechanism_as_named: Reduced Parabacteroides correlates with increased GVHD

items.quote: Lachnospiraceae and Enterococcaceae are essential to maintain GI tract integrity and facilitate immune reconstitution long-term after radiation exposure
items.location: body: Microbiota modification and HSCT outcomes
items.note: Non-GVHD outcome (GI integrity and immune reconstitution after radiation exposure, not HSCT GVHD). [90]

items.quote: We and others demonstrated in murine HSCT models that prior administration of broad spectrum antibiotics reduced acute GVHD post-allogeneic HSCT in part due to significantly decreased bacterial translocation into bloodstream
items.note: No microbial target: broad-spectrum antibiotic depletion of the whole microbiota; the surrounding MHC class II, neutrophil and T-cell migration mechanisms are likewise untargeted. [50,94]

items.quote: multiple selective microbiota alteration approaches have been extensively studied to ameliorate GVHD and improve HSCT outcomes (Figure 2)
items.note: Figure 2 (no legend in source) depicts Enterococcus and Akkermansia muciniphila with increased GVHD, and Blautia and Clostridia producing SCFAs acting on ILCs and IL-22, but carries no citations; the cited taxa are already rows from the text. Figure rule: no cited claim beyond the text.

items.quote: Vossen et al. used the combination of neomycin, polymyxin B, cephaloridin, and amphotericin B to target all bacteria, yeasts, and fungi and demonstrated reductions in both infections and GVHD in children
items.note: No microbial target: complete gut decontamination of the whole community; the follow-up decontamination study [101] fails for the same reason. [100]

items.quote: Antibiotics targeting anaerobic bacteria are associated with higher rates of GVHD-related mortality targeting the intestinal tract due to the development of mucus-degrading bacteria

fields.mechanism_as_named: Anaerobe-targeting antibiotics raise GVHD mortality via mucus-degrading bacteria

items.note: Direction read from depletion by antibiotics worsening GVHD-related mortality. Mechanism set to 3a (mucus degradation); 4a colonization resistance is a plausible alternative.

items.quote: Antibiotics targeting anaerobic bacteria are associated with higher rates of GVHD-related mortality targeting the intestinal tract due to the development of mucus-degrading bacteria

fields.mechanism_as_named: Mucus-degrading bacteria expand and raise intestinal GVHD mortality

items.note: Treated as a functional group (shared biological function: mucus degradation), which is not among the codebook's listed examples.

items.quote: Continuous prophylactic treatment using broad-spectrum antibiotic cocktail with ampicillin, vancomycin, and neomycin demonstrated a protective effect in gut permeability and GVHD outcomes in high-fat diet fed obese mice
items.note: No microbial target: broad-spectrum antibiotic effect on the whole microbiota. [50]

items.quote: butyrate, which has been shown to mitigate GVHD through the signaling by G-protein-coupled receptor 43 (GPR43) on the intestinal epithelial cells
items.note: No microbial target: metabolite (butyrate) only, no producing taxon or producer group named. [109]

items.quote: Dietary fiber changed the gut microbiota profiles by increasing diversity (Bacteroidaceae and Bifidobacteriaceae), which enhances SCFAs production
items.note: No GVHD outcome in the statement (diet effect on composition and SCFA production). [110]

items.quote: a high-fat only diet increases Bacteroides, Enterobacteriaceae, Escherichia, Klebsiella, and Shigella
items.note: Composition change with diet; no GVHD link in the statement. [111]

items.quote: contribute to the increase of genus Bifidobacterium and Lactobacilli and the decrease of the genus Bacteroides
items.note: Prebiotic effect on composition; benefit is stated for HSCT patients generally (uncited preprint DOI) or checkpoint blockade, with no GVHD outcome. [112]

items.quote: Patients that consumed prebiotics had reduced mucosal tissue damage and ameliorated acute GVHD
items.note: No microbial target: prebiotic intervention with no taxon named. [114]

items.quote: Oral administration of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG in drinking water before and after HSCT resulted in reduced bacterial translocation, improved survival, and reduced acute GVHD pathogenesis

fields.mechanism_as_named: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG probiotic reduced acute GVHD in mice

items.note: Strain GG coded at species rank (no strain rank in the codebook). Reduced bacterial translocation is listed as a co-outcome, not stated as the mechanism, so 0 rather than 3a.

items.quote: Administration of 17 butyrate-producing Clostridia spp. strains by oral gavage before and after allogeneic HSCT with an MHC mismatched model demonstrated a significant increase of butyrate in the intestine and better survival rate
items.note: Non-GVHD outcome: survival only, GVHD not named in the statement. Promote if survival in an MHC-mismatched model is read as GVHD mortality. [116]

items.quote: A cocktail of Clostridium bolteae, Ruminococcus gnavus, Ruminococcus torques, and Blautia producta delivered by oral gavage also showed significant survival in mice
items.note: Non-GVHD outcome: survival only, GVHD not named in the statement. [117]

items.quote: The use of probiotics-enriched yogurt in a case report of a patient with autologous HSCT for treating mantle-cell lymphoma resulted in unexpected Lactobacillus acidophilus sepsis
items.note: Non-GVHD outcome (sepsis) and autologous HSCT. [118]

items.quote: another clinical study reported the bloodstream infections with Lactobacillus bacteremia in patients with autologous and allogeneic HSCT within the first 100 d post-HSCT
items.note: Non-GVHD outcome (bacteremia). [119]

items.quote: administration of probiotics with Lactobacillus plantarum was safe and feasible with no bacteremia case recorded
items.note: Non-GVHD outcome (safety and bacteremia only). [120]

items.quote: Early clinical studies used FMT to treat patients with Clostridium difficile infections with high efficacy and minimal complications
items.note: Non-GVHD outcome (C. difficile infection). [121-127]

items.quote: FMT was also performed in steroid-resistant acute GVHD patients with no adverse effect and resulted in the restored microbiome diversity, an increase of peripheral regulatory T cells and better progression-free survival
items.note: Diversity only; no microbial target named. [128-130]

items.quote: when FMT was used in patients with steroid-refractory or steroid-dependent intestinal GVHD, researchers observed a significant increase of microbiome alpha-diversity, increased abundances of butyrate-producing Clostridiales and Blautia

fields.evidence_as_stated: patients with steroid-refractory or steroid-dependent intestinal GVHD
fields.mechanism_as_named: Butyrate-producing Clostridiales increased after FMT for refractory GVHD

items.note: Producer descriptor with no distinct downstream mechanism, so 1a. Direction from rise after FMT; the quote reports no clinical response, success taken from the next sentence calling FMT promising for intestinal GVHD.

items.quote: when FMT was used in patients with steroid-refractory or steroid-dependent intestinal GVHD, researchers observed a significant increase of microbiome alpha-diversity, increased abundances of butyrate-producing Clostridiales and Blautia

fields.evidence_as_stated: patients with steroid-refractory or steroid-dependent intestinal GVHD
fields.mechanism_as_named: Blautia increased after FMT for refractory GVHD

items.note: 'butyrate-producing' read as modifying Clostridiales only, so Blautia is 0; 1a if the descriptor is read as covering both. Direction as for the Clostridiales row.
